frames.narration: Processor 2 sends its file for Tuesday in the small hours of Wednesday: 1,204,331 lines in its own format, in its own time zone (UTC-8). The loader hashes the file, stores it exactly as received in the immutable file store, and records it as file f-77, version 1, for Processor 2, business day Tuesday.

Twenty minutes later the processor's retry sends the same file again. The hash is the same, so the loader records a second delivery of f-77 and loads nothing. Nothing is counted twice, and nobody has to notice.

The normalizer turns each line into the one canonical record. A sale of 20.00 with a fee column of 0.88 becomes gross 2,000, fee 88 and net 1,912 minor units of USD, type sale. A line stamped 23:40 on Tuesday in UTC-8 is Tuesday's business day for this processor, although in UTC it is already Wednesday. The original line is kept next to it.

The bank statement arrives with one payout for Processor 2's Tuesday. The service ties the file to the bank before looking at single payments: the net of all 1,204,331 lines equals the payout to the cent, so no line is missing from the file.

The partition for Processor 2 and Tuesday runs under rule version 7. 1,198,012 lines match on id and amount. 4,986 match on id within 5 cents, a fee rounding difference that is booked as a variance. 52 lines that lost their reference match on card tail and amount. 1,281 lines are left.

The leftovers are classified. 1,196 are timing: the other side is expected on Wednesday's partition, so they wait a day. 41 are chargeback lines the ledger never recorded, a status break, and 44 are missing on one side. The 41 go to the disputes team, and the 3 largest of the 44, over 1,000.00 each, go first to a senior analyst, with their age starting now.

An analyst opens a chargeback of 148.20. The processor withdrew the money on a dispute, and the ledger has the sale as settled. She approves a proposal: a balanced entry that debits the dispute-loss account and credits the processor receivable by 14,820. The poster sends it to the ledger with the break id as its idempotency key, so a repeat of the same message posts nothing new.

By morning the remaining breaks are either repaired or approved to carry, so the unexplained money is zero and Tuesday closes with the files and rule version it used on record. At noon the processor sends a corrected file that supersedes 3 rows. The partition runs again, the old result is kept, and the difference is posted as new entries, because Tuesday was already closed.
